x: What are skills? Skills are folders with instructions, scripts and files that Claude loads when they're needed. A skill is a folder with instructions (and sometimes scripts and example files) that teaches Claude how to do a particular task well and consistently. Think of a work instruction you give a new colleague: this is how we make a newsletter , this is our house style , this is how you test this app . The clever part: Claude only loads a skill when it needs it . Of every skill, Claude first sees only the name and a short description. Only when your question matches does it read the full instructions. That's why you can install dozens of skills without Claude getting slower or more confused. What does a skill look like? my-skill/ ├── SKILL.md ← required: description + instructions ├── examples/ ← optional: example files └── scripts/ ← optional: scripts Claude may run SKILL.md --- name: neighbourhood-newsletter description: Writes the monthly newsletter of the neighbourhood council in our fixed structure. Use for every request for a newsletter, neighbourhood update or announcement to residents. --- # Neighbourhood newsletter 1. Start with a short personal opening (max. 3 sentences). 2. Then the fixed sections: News, Agenda, Call to action, Contact. 3. Write in plain language and address the reader as 'you'. x: Install safely Skills can contain instructions and scripts. This is how to install them safely. A skill tells Claude what to do, and can contain scripts that Claude runs. So only install skills you trust. ★ Watch out for fake copies. Of popular skills like Humanizer, copies that look identical are circulating on GitHub. Always install from the repo the author names themselves. Checklist ☐ Does the skill come from a known author or an official marketplace? ☐ Have you read the SKILL.md ? Is there nothing odd in it, like 'send files to…'? ☐ Does the skill contain scripts? Have a quick look at what they do. ☐ Is there allowed-tools in the frontmatter? Claude may use those tools without asking. ☐ Does the plugin have hooks ? They run automatically on certain events. ☐ Does data go to an external service (as with debate skills or hosted memory services)? Then don't put sensitive information in it. Official vs. community Official (Anthropic) Community Where anthropics/skills , claude-plugins-official All other repos Reviewed Made or included by Anthropic No, your own responsibility Quality Stable From brilliant to messy i Even for the official marketplace, Anthropic warns: make sure you trust a plugin before installing it . Partner plugins can contain MCP servers and software that Anthropic does not control.

x: Frequently asked questions Frequently asked questions about Claude skills: what they cost, installing them, the Claude app versus Claude Code and sharing with your team. Do skills cost money? The skills themselves are almost always free. In the Claude app you do need a Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise plan. Some skills use external services (like Remotion for large companies or hosted memory services) with their own terms. Does a skill from Claude Code also work in the Claude app? Often it does: it's the same standard. Zip the skill folder and upload it. Skills that depend on **hooks**, local programs or the terminal only work in Claude Code. How many skills can I install? Plenty. Claude first only sees the name and description and loads the rest only when needed. Too many skills with overlapping descriptions can cause confusion though: clean up what you don't use. My skill isn't being used. What now? 1. Check that it is enabled (`/plugin` in Claude Code, Settings → Capabilities in the app). 2. Restart Claude Code. 3.
